notes:
The complete 79158-character markdown conversion of the 13-page journal article was read from beginning through the references, including all end matter. There is no appendix in the saved document. PDF text on pp. 4-5, 11 and 13 was checked with PyMuPDF; all PDF link annotations and embedded-file names were inspected. No data/code/materials availability statement, on-request offer, preregistration statement, supplementary-file notice, or study repository link was found. The p. 11 acknowledgments thank participants, and the ethics statement promises anonymity and confidentiality; neither specifies data access. The statements list therefore contains no availability quotations. Methods, Materials (pp. 4-5) describes author-made visual stimuli reproduced in Figures 1-2, and Figure 5 (p. 9) gives an illustrative AI-generated design example. These in-article illustrations and the aggregate results in Tables 1-2 are not a participant-level dataset or a complete collection of participant outputs. The PDF has no embedded files. The article's CC BY 4.0 notice is an article license, not evidence of a separately licensed dataset.

The paper DOI https://doi.org/10.1017/S0890060425100061 returned HTTP 200 after redirecting to https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/ai-edam/article/effects-of-generative-ai-model-type-and-visual-stimuli-type-on-design-creativity/BA8DEA8280F01CF33050317ECE20975A ; a direct request to that publisher landing page also returned HTTP 200. The publisher HTML contains supplementaryMaterials:[] and only Article, Figures, and Metrics tabs. No article-specific supplementary data or repository links were present. Its Publishing supplementary material link is a general publisher help page, not a supplement for this paper. Bibliographic references, author ORCID, and article-license links are not study deposits.

The form's data_and_code.data_url and code_url are empty. S1 is the only study in the form; random assignment is not stated. The actual form has no final object or final.open_items field. Its open_questions instead identify unreported analyzed counts and conflicting reported effects, among other design uncertainties. No public participant-level or participant-linked output data were located, so no missing arm means, SDs, SEs, analyzed counts, or diversity measures can be computed from a confirmed public deposit, and conflicting reported statistics cannot be resolved from raw data. No dataset columns or participant rows were available to inspect. Unrelated search hits are documented in searches and are not counted as deposits.

The required title and first-author searches were completed through the named APIs using urllib and User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1. Zenodo's initial HTTP 400 responses were page-size validation errors, resolved by using the permitted public size=25; they do not establish restricted access. OSF's later broad-search timeouts were resolved by pagination. No login or access request was used. Confidence is medium because the paper, publisher page, and searches support none_found, while a differently named or unindexed deposit remains possible.
